description: Hi! I’m interested in AI, coding, satellite data, and space technology. I enjoy using technology to solve real-world problems. I’m looking for teammates with skills in programming, AI, data analysis, design, or research. Creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn are also very welcome!
summary:
When a storm passes, it can be hard to tell which fields need attention first. We built SAR2Action to help people investigate these changes using satellite radar.

Our platform brings together NASA–ISRO NISAR observations, NASA's OPERA radar products derived from Sentinel-1, and agricultural data from Taiwan. Users can explore an interactive map, compare radar observations from different dates, and see where changes occurred. The system also estimates how much mapped farmland overlaps areas with unusual radar signals.

We added an AI assistant to help users examine the evidence, consider possible explanations, and look up relevant agricultural relief information.

We started with Yunlin, Taiwan, and designed the system to work with data from other regions. Since a change in radar signals does not necessarily mean crops were damaged, we keep observations separate from conclusions that still need verification.

Our goal is to make satellite data easier to use when deciding which agricultural areas may need further investigation.
details:
SAR2Action: Mapping Changes in Farmland with Satellite Radar

1. The Problem and Our Solution

Extreme weather can cause widespread agricultural damage, while traditional field inspections require significant time and resources. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can observe Earth's surface regardless of cloud cover or daylight, making it valuable for disaster monitoring.

Developed by Team SARAPHIM, SAR2Action is an interactive geospatial platform that transforms satellite radar observations into traceable agricultural change-screening evidence. Our goal is to help farmers, researchers, and authorities identify areas requiring further investigation.

2. NASA Data and Methodology

NASA–ISRO NISAR: We use L-band HH/HV observations from October 4 and 16, 2026, to establish a pre-event radar reference.

NASA OPERA RTC-S1: We analyze Sentinel-1 C-band VV/VH observations from October 14 and 26, 2026, to screen agricultural surface changes across a storm period.

Our Yunlin County case study covers 4,863 farmland parcels, identifying 181 radar-change candidates for further inspection.

These observations represent radar changes, not confirmed crop damage. NISAR and Sentinel-1 measurements are interpreted separately due to differences in sensor characteristics and acquisition conditions.

3. Platform Features and Technologies

SAR2Action integrates an interactive WebGIS with farmland visualization, evidence-based investigation, WGS84/TWD97 coordinate transformation, polygon drawing, area measurement, and GeoJSON import/export.

The platform also provides conditional agricultural disaster relief calculations based on Taiwan's regulations. These estimates are for reference only and do not determine official eligibility.

Our investigation workflow organizes information into Observed, Inferred, and Unknown categories, with evidence references and tool execution records. Gemini Function Calling has been integrated as an optional capability, although live execution has not yet been fully verified.

The system was developed using Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, MapLibre, GDAL, Shapely, and pyproj, with AI-assisted development tools.

4. Innovation and Impact

SAR2Action goes beyond satellite image visualization by connecting radar-change screening with interactive geographic analysis, scientific evidence, and practical agricultural decision support.

Its key strengths are accessibility, traceability, and responsible interpretation.

The platform can help agricultural authorities and field inspectors prioritize investigations, while making complex radar observations easier for non-specialists to understand.

5. Limitations and Future Development

Radar changes may result from soil moisture, crop growth, harvesting, or other environmental factors. Our current observations cannot independently confirm storm-induced crop damage, actual loss rates, or official compensation eligibility.

Future development will integrate Copernicus Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, including NDVI, NDRE, and LSWI, alongside cloud-quality screening and field observations. We also plan to strengthen multi-sensor analysis, improve AI-assisted investigation, and expand to additional agricultural regions.
